findings.title: Compile error: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() called with no arguments
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with zero arguments. The only method with that name visible via the inherited UsernamePasswordForm class is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, which requires a `UserModel` parameter. There is no no-arg overload anywhere in the class hierarchy shown in this PR (AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator doesn't define one either). This call therefore cannot be resolved and the module will fail to compile ('method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled in class UsernamePasswordForm cannot be applied to given types'). The call was most likely meant to be `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, matching the pattern used elsewhere (e.g. UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate()/challenge()).

findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) requires a non-null user, inverting the WebAuthn conditional-UI setup and breaking normal (non-reauthentication) passkey login
findings.body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns true only when `user != null`. It gates the call to `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` both in `authenticate()` (line 115) and in the overridden `challenge(context, error, field)` (line 137); `fillContextForm` populates the WebAuthn challenge/rpId/conditional-UI attributes that enable the browser's passkey autofill UI on the combined username/password form. Before this change, that call ran precisely when `context.getUser() == null` (the normal/first-time login path, with no pre-selected user) — this is the primary use case for discoverable-credential/passkey autofill login, and was explicitly commented as 'setup webauthn data when the user is not already selected'. After the change, the call only fires when a user is already set (the new re-authentication scenario this PR targets), so for every normal fresh login attempt (no pre-selected user) the WebAuthn attributes are never populated and passkeys conditional UI will not be offered — this removes functionality rather than adding the new re-authentication support, and conflicts with existing/updated tests that still expect the webauthn form/autofill to appear for fresh, non-reauthenticated logins (e.g. PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest#webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey, PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest's non-discoverable-key flow). The fix for re-authentication should be additive to, not a replacement for, the existing null-user case.

findings.title: Unused import left after assertions were changed
findings.body: The import `org.openqa.selenium.NoSuchElementException` is no longer referenced anywhere in the file: both previous usages inside `passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey` (`Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, () -> ...)`) were replaced with `MatcherAssert.assertThat(..., Matchers.notNullValue())` in this PR. The now-dead import should be removed; in modules where checkstyle enforces 'no unused imports' this would fail the build.
